blocks.text:
This extensive group itinerary travels through Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Over 18 days, you will see Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago and the Atacama Desert, high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz and Lake Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

The programme forms one continuous journey, connecting domestic flights, transfers, tours and journeys through the Andes. City days alternate with time in nature: Rio’s ocean coast, tropical waterfalls, desert, salt flats, high-altitude lakes and ancient Inca cities.

## What the journey includes

The first days in Brazil are spent in Rio de Janeiro. Ascend Corcovado to the statue of Christ the Redeemer and Sugar Loaf Mountain, and discover historic neighbourhoods and the Atlantic coast.

The route then continues to Iguazu. You will see the falls from both sides of the border. The Brazilian side offers a wide panorama of the cascades, while paths and bridges on the Argentine side bring you closer to the torrents and the Devil’s Throat.

In Argentina, the programme focuses on Buenos Aires: Plaza de Mayo, La Boca, San Telmo, Puerto Madero, Recoleta, the Obelisk and an evening tango show.

The Andean section begins next. Discover Santiago’s historic centre and modern districts, then fly to Calama and continue to San Pedro de Atacama.

The following days are spent at high altitude. The jeep route through Bolivia passes Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers, Laguna Colorada and a series of high-altitude lagoons. Then head onto the Uyuni Salt Flat to see Colchani, the Ojos del Salar (“Eyes of Water”) and Incahuasi Island with its giant cacti.

A flight from Uyuni to La Paz is included in the itinerary. After exploring the city, the Witches’ Market and the Valley of the Moon, continue via Tiwanaku towards Lake Titicaca and Peru.

The final section takes you through Puno, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

## How the journey changes from country to country

The first 6 days reveal 2 different sides of Brazil. Rio centres on city panoramas, the ocean and historic neighbourhoods. Iguazu, by contrast, focuses almost entirely on nature. From the Brazilian side, the falls first appear as one immense system; on the Argentine side, you approach individual cascades more closely.

Buenos Aires is a short but eventful city stop. Its old districts, central squares, modern waterfront and an evening of tango are brought together in 1 day. This change of scene provides a different pace before Chile and the high-altitude section that follows.

Santiago introduces Chile through its city centre, La Moneda, Plaza de Armas and modern districts. The programme then heads far from the capital into the Atacama. After flying to Calama, continue to San Pedro de Atacama, where the dry, clear air and night sky contrast sharply with humid Rio and Iguazu.

The stop in San Pedro also allows time for acclimatisation. The next section travels at altitudes of around 3800–4400 m. Altitude sickness is possible, so this part of the journey calls for a gentler pace.

The Bolivian section begins after crossing the border in 4x4 jeeps. The landscape combines high-altitude plains, coloured lagoons, volcanoes, hot springs and geysers. Licancabur volcano rises beside Laguna Verde, rock formations stand in the Dalí Desert, and at Sol de Mañana the earth releases hot jets and thermal mud.

Laguna Colorada lies at an altitude of 4400 m. Its red water and James’s flamingos make this one of the route’s most unusual sights. The night is spent in a simple hotel on the desert plateau; in terms of conditions, this day comes closest to an expedition.

The following day gradually brings you to Uyuni. Before reaching the salt flat, the route passes the lagoons of Honda, Chiarkota, Hedionda and Cañapa, the viewpoint by Ollagüe volcano and the Chiguana salt flats. Uyuni itself changes with the season: a dry white surface or an immense reflecting mirror in the rainy season.

In Colchani, you can see salt being extracted. The Ojos del Salar reveal places where water rises through the salt surface, while Incahuasi Island is known for its giant cacti. Lunch is provided as a lunch box that day.

La Paz brings you back to an urban setting, now against an Andean backdrop. The Witches’ Market introduces local traditions, while the Valley of the Moon reveals unusual terrain shaped by water and wind.

The road from Bolivia to Peru passes through Tiwanaku. This is an important stop before the border: the Gate of the Sun, Kalasasaya and the ancient structures reveal Andean history before the Incas. After crossing the border, arrive in Puno and visit the floating Uros Islands that same day.

The journey from Puno to Cusco takes a full day, broken up by stops. Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani, the La Raya Pass and Pucará make the road a distinct part of the trip. The final 3 days then remain: Machu Picchu, Cusco and its archaeological complexes, and Lima before your international flight.

## Altitudes and journeys

The highest sections begin in the Atacama and continue into Peru. Uyuni lies at around 3650 m, Laguna Colorada at 4400 m, and the La Raya Pass also at 4400 m. The programme moves progressively through these places rather than making a sudden day trip up from a coastal city.

Domestic flights connect the most distant points, while overland journeys are used where the road itself is part of the programme. This is why the Bolivian section uses jeeps, while Puno and Cusco are linked by a tourist bus with stops.

## Prices per person in USD

The base price is USD 8,945 per person for 2 participants sharing a double room in the first hotel category. For 3 participants sharing a triple room (TRL), the rate is USD 8,005 per person. Domestic flights are included. SGL means single occupancy, DBL a place in a double room, and TRL a place in a triple room.
